Retain the in-force condition while returning the evidence, uncertainty, burden and protected-function comparison to its competent owner. A favorable resource argument alone never grants a waiver.

### RMP.6:6 - Bias-Annotation

| Recurring bias | Likely drift | Corrective move |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Repetition bias | Any repeat is treated as a stronger test of the substantive claim. | Name the precise relation being challenged and the result that could change it. |
| Favorable-outcome bias | Criteria or tested variants are selected after seeing agreement. | Preserve the intended criterion, justified changes and unexamined range. |
| Quantity-of-methods bias | More Methods or sources are treated as independent support. | Recover their distinct contributions, dependence and disagreement logic. |
| Acquisition bias | Every remaining uncertainty becomes another study. | Compare attainable contribution with the full arrangement and allow a bounded completion. |
| Authority shortcut | A requirement is defended by its label or bypassed because it is costly. | Examine protection merits separately from the competent decision and current force. |

### RMP.6:7 - Conformance Checklist

Apply these questions to the current credibility decision and any actual return, not to an imagined complete battery of tests.

- [ ] Direct entry identifies the bounded claim, current basis, proposed use and live threat.
- [ ] The selected question has a possible result that can change the claim or useful next move.
- [ ] An adequate existing examination can complete the question without an unused test inventory.
- [ ] Reproduction, replication, robustness, validation, corroboration and transfer retain their different comparisons and limits.
- [ ] The Method, relevant correspondence and criterion make the selected examination interpretable.
- [ ] Real alternatives are compared without a numerical quota or universal credibility score.
- [ ] Contribution is compared with complete obtainable burden, shared resources, protection and displaced work.
- [ ] A no-new-test answer preserves insufficient evidence or uncertainty where it remains.
- [ ] A missing-input return names the dependent selection without commissioning acquisition.
- [ ] The test decision, specification, actual performance and returned result remain distinct.
- [ ] Agreement, discrepancy, inconclusiveness and inability to attempt or interpret are not conflated.
- [ ] A disputed requirement receives a protected-function and burden comparison while current authority remains intact.
- [ ] The receiving answer retains its material qualification and the relevant exact return.

### RMP.6:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Anti-pattern | Why it fails | Practical correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| “The rerun validates the model” | The computation can agree while the intended-use relation remains unsupported. | Select the examination of that relation under supplied criteria. |
| “The replication was not significant, so the effect is absent” | The label omits magnitude, uncertainty and the chosen comparison. | Interpret the actual result under its design and criterion. |
| “Many copies corroborate the source” | Repeated carriers can preserve one dependent account. | Examine origin, dependence and the distinct evidential contribution. |
| “No data access means the claim failed” | An unattemptable comparison supplies no contrary output. | Return the access limit and the exact examination still unavailable. |
| “Each test fits, so the programme fits” | Shared demands can exceed the total available arrangement. | Check admitted joint combinations and choose a feasible useful set. |
| “We selected the test, so credibility increased” | A prospective decision supplies no performed result. | Keep the claim's current support unchanged until actual evidence warrants revision. |
| “It is required, therefore it protects” | Current force does not establish incremental protection. | Examine merits and return amendment to its responsible authority. |

### RMP.6:9 - Consequences

Credibility work becomes a contribution to a stated claim rather than a ritual sequence. Useful existing results can finish the question; newly obtainable comparisons can justify further work. Access failures, discrepancies and uncertainty remain interpretable instead of being converted into blanket verdicts.

The cost is judgement about the comparison, disciplinary criteria and full arrangement. Some tests remain unavailable, and some attractive claims remain unsupported. A qualified completion makes that boundary usable without removing an authority's legitimate requirement.

### RMP.6:10 - Rationale

A credibility test is informative through the relation between its possible result and the claim. That relation explains both why one well-targeted comparison can matter and why a battery of mismatched tests can add little.

Evidence adequacy and acquisition choice are different questions. Preserving both allows a researcher to finish the present allocation honestly while keeping uncertainty visible. Separating prospective decisions from actual results prevents an approved study plan from being mistaken for support.

Protective requirements also make distinct claims about value, causal or measurement effects, practical burden and authority. Examining one does not automatically establish or cancel the others.

### RMP.6:11 - SoTA-Echoing

The working question is which examination can improve or revise confidence in a bounded research claim, under what criterion, and at what obtainable burden.

The [National Academies' 2019 synthesis](https://doi.org/10.17226/25303) supplies the useful distinction between computational reproduction and new-data replication. It remains an anchor rather than a universal ladder.

The 2026 SCORE accounts refine different questions in social and behavioural research. The [reproducibility study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10203-5) distinguishes availability of usable data from computational reproduction. The [replicability study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-10078-y) makes differing success criteria consequential. The [analytical-robustness study](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09844-9) examines defensible analytical alternatives. RMP.6 retains those distinctions without importing the studies' sampled fields, rates or tolerances as universal criteria.

[Braun and Clarke's qualitative guidance](https://www.thematicanalysis.net/editor-checklist/) and [2024 RTARG account](https://doi.org/10.1177/02692163241234800) preserve methodological coherence for reflexive thematic analysis. The [American Historical Association's standards](https://www.historians.org/resource/statement-on-standards-of-professional-conduct/) retain source integrity and criticism for historical claims. Neither implies that all credibility questions should use the same repetition or agreement procedure.

The [2021 MRC framework](https://www.bmj.com/content/374/bmj.n2061) supports question-dependent perspectives, context and research's resource consequences in complex-intervention research. RMP.6 carries that contrast into the local choice without imposing intervention phases on every domain.

These sources do not supply the actual data, domain threshold, empirical result or authority. Reopen the affected comparison when a stronger methodological account, changed source, criterion, obtainable arrangement or receiving use changes what the test could establish.

### RMP.6:12 - Relations

- **RMP.5:** supplies a bounded claim and criticism or receives a claim whose support changed; compatible direct inputs also allow entry.
- **RMP.2:** selects a new or revised research design when the credibility question requires one. Its no-new-study answer does not imply a selected test or design.
- **RMP.3 and RMP.4:** supply the consequential operational specification and actual trace needed for a selected examination; neither creates its result in advance.
- **RMP.1:** qualifies a materially changed research question or supplies an exact ordinary-practice or source return.
- **FPF A.10 and A.10.1:** govern claim-bound evidence use and revalidation of affected uses when a relied-on source changes. **C.11.DUA and A.15.9:** govern decision-useful evidence demands and obtaining a bounded result from another practice, including attainable contribution and whole burden. The research-specific comparison remains here.
- **Domain and receiving practices:** supply Methods, criteria, protection and permissions, and retain the value, action and amendment decisions.

- **RMP.7 and RMP.8:** an actual credibility result can supply compatible corpus appraisal or exact claim/model revision and evidence return. A selected test alone supplies neither result. An adequate credibility answer can still finish directly.

### RMP.6:End

# Part IV - Synthesize Evidence and Revise the Exact Contribution


## RMP.7 - Synthesize a Research Evidence Corpus

> **Status:** Stable

> **Type:** Research Method Practice practitioner method pattern

### RMP.7:1 - Problem Frame

Use this pattern when several research reports, source interpretations or an existing synthesis bear on a question, and someone needs to determine **what their combined contribution warrants**. Start by stating the question the synthesis must answer and checking what the supplied corpus actually contains. Reuse an adequate existing synthesis.

Four reports can represent only two independent tests plus a different kind of material. Several historical accounts can repeat one memoir. Studies can disagree because their questions or settings differ. The useful first result separates these relations before treating apparent agreement as stronger support.

This Method produces an **EvidenceSynthesis**: the warranted corpus answer, how the contributions were related, and the limits needed for criticism and reuse. A short answer linked to an existing review may suffice. A new analysis may need a study map, comparison or computation; the result name requires no universal database or dossier.

Enter directly with a qualified question, applicable synthesis design, operational choices and trace adequate for this use, whether supplied or developed through RMP.1–RMP.4. A design may permit reasoned refinement as historical or qualitative material becomes understood. Preserve the resulting question and criticism, or explicitly return the changed premise.

Use the relevant source Method when finding or comparing sources already closes the question. Use RMP.5 for a particular material-to-claim inference. RMP.7 adds the research-specific difficulty of appraisal and integration across a corpus. A missing disciplinary synthesis Method, inaccessible decisive material or unsettled question returns to its supplier with the affected conclusion identified.

### RMP.7:2 - Problem

A collection can look like a body of corroborating evidence while sharing one underlying study, selecting favorable results or combining incompatible claims. A pooled number can conceal that its inputs measure different things. A common theme can conceal a consequential difference in setting or meaning.

The opposite response is to abandon every synthesis that contains disagreement or imperfect sources. That discards compatible quantitative combination, a useful interpretive account or a precise explanation of what the corpus cannot establish. Another unnecessary cost is recreating an adequate review merely to produce a new dated record.

The practitioner needs a corpus answer whose form follows the research question, the source relations and the criticism that matters.

### RMP.7:3 - Forces

| Force | Tension |
| --- | --- |
| Joint support | More contributions can strengthen an inference, while repeated material can create only the appearance of corroboration. |
| A concise answer | A synthesis reduces reading effort, while an aggregate may erase the contrast the receiver needs. |
| Different traditions | Quantitative, interpretive and historical inquiries can inform one question, while their transformations and confidence claims differ. |
| Coverage | Relevant omissions can change a finding, while a complete search may exceed what a bounded question needs or what access permits. |
| Reuse and change | An existing synthesis saves work, while a changed source, question or use can invalidate part of it. |
| Completion | A qualified corpus answer can finish, while a worthwhile new inquiry remains a separate choice. |

### RMP.7:4 - Solution

Recover the question and actual corpus, distinguish the contributions and their dependence, appraise the inference each can support, and perform the justified synthesis. Return the answer with its consequential transformations, uncertainty and scope.

#### RMP.7:4.1 - State the question and test the supplied answer

Name the subject, comparison or interpretive concern, relevant context and period, and the kind of conclusion wanted. A mean difference, explanation, account of experiences and claim about a historical sequence ask different questions even when they concern the same topic.

Inspect any supplied synthesis for the same question, relevant source coverage, Method, actual findings, limitations and current receiving use. If it already supplies an adequate answer, return that answer with the source and qualifications that change reliance. Reopen only a changed premise or uncovered question.

Otherwise establish the actual source set against the selected design: what was eligible, sought, obtained, excluded or unavailable, and why those choices bear on this answer. Systematic-coverage claims need the corresponding search and selection work. A deliberately bounded corpus can answer its bounded question without claiming to represent every study.

Return a changed question to RMP.1, an unsettled synthesis design to RMP.2, an operational problem to RMP.3 or an actual-material problem to RMP.4. An adequate supplied input needs no recreation of those earlier activities.

#### RMP.7:4.2 - Recover distinct contributions before counting support

Distinguish a report from its underlying studies and material, a source author's interpretation from the material it interprets, and either from the proposed synthesis finding.

| Source relation | Consequence for synthesis |
| --- | --- |
| Several reports concern one study | Combine their useful information into the study's contribution; resolve discrepancies and retain supplementary detail. Repeated reports do not supply independent study estimates. |
| One report contains several studies | Recover the actual studies and their relation; the document count does not determine the number of independent contributions. |
| Samples, controls, records or data overlap | Preserve the overlap and use an analysis that accounts for it, or a justified selection or grouping. A different title or author list does not establish independence. |
| Later accounts copy or interpret one earlier source | Recover the common source and the distinct interpretations. Copying is evidence of transmission; independent corroboration needs an independent evidential contribution. |
| A source adds context or a different outcome | Retain that contribution for the question it can answer. Its usefulness does not make it another estimate of the same quantity. |

Keep contrary findings and disagreements between reports visible. If dependence cannot be recovered well enough for the intended combination, qualify or withhold that combination and state what comparison remains possible.

#### RMP.7:4.3 - Appraise support for the proposed findings

Use the criteria appropriate to the research tradition and each finding. Distinguish limitations within a study, dependence among contributions, selective availability across the corpus and applicability to the synthesis question. Their effects can differ across outcomes and interpretations.

Examine consequential exclusions and missing material. Distinguish evidence that was never sought, an eligible result not reported, a lost record and a source that cannot be accessed. Identify which conclusion might change; absence from the available corpus alone does not establish an absent effect, event or experience.

A large number of publications cannot repair common dependence. A global rating for each source cannot substitute for the relation that warrants an inference. Some weaker material may still provide context or challenge an interpretation; keep its supported role and limits explicit.

An individual claim defeated by its material or Method returns to RMP.5. Use RMP.6 when a remaining credibility choice can change the present synthesis or a worthwhile next move. Selecting an examination supplies no result from an examination not yet performed.

#### RMP.7:4.4 - Perform the synthesis the question permits

Apply a qualified disciplinary Method. Explain consequential grouping, transformation, weighting or translation so that another reader can recover how source contributions became the finding.

| Question and material | Positive move | What the result may claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compatible quantitative estimates | Establish the target quantity, units, contrast, timing, dependence and uncertainty. Fit the justified statistical model and examine influential assumptions. | An estimate for that target with its warranted uncertainty and scope. A common-effect and a distributional-effect analysis have different assumptions and interpretations. |
| Quantitative findings without a justified common aggregate | Group and tabulate the relevant results; perform the supported comparison or synthesis without meta-analysis. Explain the specific missing relation that prevents the requested aggregate. | The narrower comparison actually supported, including a useful refusal of an unsupported pooled magnitude. Counting statistically significant reports does not supply it. |
| Qualitative or interpretive findings | Compare, translate or develop interpretations under the selected tradition, retaining context, source concepts, disconfirming material and the synthesist's contribution. | A descriptive synthesis or explicitly developed explanatory construct with its grounding and applicable confidence account. |
| Historical sources and accounts | Relate provenance, dating, purpose, perspective, dependence, silence and rival interpretations to the disputed chronology or explanation. | The sequence or explanation the sources warrant, with unresolved alternatives retained. |
| Mixed evidence about one question | Justify the transformation that makes contributions comparable; preserve original values, meanings and context where transformation loses detail. | An integrated answer only to the shared question the transformation supports. |
| Mixed evidence about different aspects | Synthesize each aspect on its own terms, then explain their relationship. | Convergence, complementarity or unresolved divergence without forcing unlike answers into one quantity. |

Variation does not automatically prohibit pooling; the question and model determine what variation means. Conversely, choosing a random-effects label does not make different targets compatible. A direction-only synthesis cannot estimate an effect's magnitude.

For qualitative synthesis, a participant's account, the source author's interpretation and a new synthesis construct retain their distinct contributions. When GRADE-CERQual fits the selected use, judge each qualitative finding through methodological limitations, coherence, adequacy and relevance. Its confidence terms are not numerical truth probabilities or a universal historical scale.

If the needed Method or a decisive premise is unavailable, return that specific gap and the bounded result still warranted. A polished common format cannot supply the missing inference.

#### RMP.7:4.5 - Return the useful corpus answer

State what the corpus establishes first. Include the question, material and Method actually used, consequential dependence and transformations, uncertainty, missing contributions and transfer limits that change interpretation.

Use existing source notes, an analysis output or a concise linked explanation when adequate. Preserve access conditions and enough connection to source material for the named criticism. A public synthesis and a critic's permitted access may support different examinations.

Finish with the adequate existing synthesis, the produced finding, a qualified corpus answer, an informative refusal, or a precise input return. An unanswered broader question can remain visible. Further inquiry earns selection through its attainable contribution and whole burden; insufficient evidence remains insufficient when no additional work is selected.

Use RMP.8 when the answer requires reconciliation with a wider claim or model, or a return to an actual receiving use with consequential reliance conditions. An already sufficient answer can be returned directly.

### RMP.7:5 - Archetypal Grounding

These constructed cases illustrate the Method; they report no performed study.

#### RMP.7:5.1 - Two compatible tests among four reports

A seal engineer receives reports A, A2, B and C. A/A2 describe the same randomized accelerated test; A2 supplies its fuller outcome account. B describes an independent test of the same material contrast under compatible stress and measurement conditions. C describes in-service replacement choices under different conditions.

The synthesis question is the difference in mean time to the defined laboratory failure between the new and comparison seal under the specified accelerated conditions. Assume complete observed lifetimes, suitable approximately normal estimates, independent study estimates and a domain-justified common effect. The four-report map retains A2's useful information without adding another independent estimate; C cannot estimate this laboratory contrast.

The recovered study estimates are 14 hours with standard error 4 for A/A2, and 8 hours with standard error 3 for B. Inverse-variance weights are 1/16 and 1/9. Their weighted estimate is 10.16 hours; its standard error is 2.4 hours, giving an approximate normal 95% interval of 5.46 to 14.86 hours.

The returned answer is a positive mean difference under the named laboratory conditions and assumptions. The study-specific estimates remain visible. The synthesis does not establish that the acceleration relation transfers to service or that a maintenance interval should change. C remains useful material for a different service-use question. An inadequate common-effect premise would reopen this calculation's interpretation, even if the arithmetic were correct.

#### RMP.7:5.2 - A refusal with useful content

Another supplied corpus reports leakage after one hour, failure time under another stress and technicians' replacement decisions. The requested answer is a common percentage reduction in 500-hour failure risk.

RMP.7 shows each result with its actual outcome, contrast, conditions and uncertainty. No supplied relation converts them to the requested risk. The result therefore says that this corpus does not establish that percentage and preserves the narrower comparisons it does support. It supplies neither a pooled number nor a conclusion of no effect. If the receiver asked only whether this corpus establishes the percentage, that question is complete.

#### RMP.7:5.3 - Situated participation and a mixed question

A resident group asks what impedes participation in water monitoring. One interview study links distrust to withheld feedback. Another interpretive study relates continued participation to community authority over the question. A survey reports stated reasons within its own sampled group.

Under a justified same-question mixed design, the synthesist retains the survey's counts and denominator, the qualitative contexts and the source authors' interpretations. A comparison suggests that control over both the question and returned information may matter. That explanatory connection is the synthesist's contribution; it is not a measured population prevalence. A contrary case with continued participation despite withheld feedback qualifies the explanation.

For a separate question about the monitoring intervention's effect on water quality, these accounts and any effect studies need their own syntheses before their relationship is examined. Agreement about participation is not an estimated effect on water quality.

#### RMP.7:5.4 - Shared memoir and contrary chronology

Several later histories attribute a factory's decision to close to a public protest. Their references lead to one retrospective memoir. An authenticated record dates that decision before the protest.

The historian separates the shared evidential source from the later interpretations and examines what the decision record establishes. The protest cannot have caused that earlier decision. The decision's cause and any effect on later implementation remain unresolved. The chronology is a useful completed corpus answer; counting the later histories would have concealed its decisive contradiction.

### RMP.7:6 - Bias-Annotation

The numerical example makes statistical combination unusually easy: compatible targets, recovered dependence and justified assumptions are supplied. Real corpora may require domain expertise, additional source recovery or a narrower answer. The historical and participation cases expose different criteria; neither makes this pattern an exhaustive handbook for those traditions.

Publication and access practices can privilege certain institutions, languages or surviving sources. Interpret silence and corpus coverage in that setting. Reusing a convenient synthesis remains appropriate only for the question and qualifications it actually covers.

### RMP.7:7 - Conformance Checklist

Use these questions to examine a proposed synthesis after recognizing the corpus difficulty:

- Can the receiver recover the exact question and why an existing answer does or does not suffice?
- Are reports, underlying studies or material, source interpretations and synthesis findings distinguishable, including consequential dependence?
- Do eligibility, exclusions, missing material and access limits support the stated corpus scope?
- Does each consequential transformation have a Method and an interpretation that fit its question?
- Are contrary findings, uncertainty and transfer limits retained at the findings they affect?
- Does the answer finish the bounded use or return the specific missing result without disguising an unperformed inquiry as evidence?

Recognition selects this Method. These questions examine the resulting synthesis; recognition alone does not establish its adequacy.

### RMP.7:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Failure | What changes in practice |
| --- | --- |
| More reports are treated as more independent studies. | Recover the underlying contributions and model or remove double counting while retaining supplementary information. |
| Everything numerical is pooled. | Recover the target and transformation; use a supported narrower synthesis when they do not justify the requested aggregate. |
| Only significant findings count as agreement. | Synthesize the relevant estimates or other justified contribution, retaining uncertainty and missing evidence. |
| A theme becomes a population percentage. | Preserve the qualitative interpretation and use actual sampling and measurement support for a prevalence claim. |
| A single confidence label covers the whole corpus. | Tie appraisal and uncertainty to the finding and the approach whose criteria supply that judgment. |
| Disagreement prevents any useful answer. | State the supported distinctions or the precise refusal, including what remains unresolved. |

### RMP.7:9 - Consequences

The practitioner can return a defensible corpus answer while preserving useful differences between sources. Compatible contributions can strengthen an estimate; unlike or dependent contributions can instead change its scope, explanation or limits.

The cost is question-specific appraisal and explicit consequential transformations. Adequate-synthesis reuse and proportionate records reduce work without turning incomplete evidence into a stronger claim.

### RMP.7:10 - Rationale

A source collection supplies material; the research synthesis establishes a further relation among its contributions. That relation needs its own design and criticism. Keeping it distinct from RMP.5's individual inference makes dependence, coverage and integration visible without making synthesis compulsory after every analysis.

A useful refusal is informative when it identifies the missing relation and preserves the supported answer. It protects both legitimate combination and honest completion.

### RMP.7:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**What counts as independent support?** The selected line recovers the underlying studies and source relationships while retaining additional information from their reports. The cheap default is to count publications or discard all apparent duplicates. The former inflates support; the latter can lose follow-up detail. **Adapt:** 4.2 combines information at the appropriate contribution and preserves consequential overlap, as illustrated by A/A2 in 5.1. Cochrane [chapter 5](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-05) supplies the best-known-line candidate for these report/study distinctions because it resolves both failures, not because it is an institutional handbook. This recovery adds work when relationships are unclear; it is needed only where they can change the finding. New overlap, provenance or supplementary results reopen the affected contribution.

**Which numerical answer can this corpus support?** The selected line chooses a synthesis for a stated quantity and dependence model, with explicit alternatives when that quantity is unsupported. The serious alternatives are pooling every numerical result or refusing all heterogeneous material. The first invents comparability; the second can discard a warranted combined estimate. **Adapt:** 4.4 and 5.1–5.2 preserve justified combination and an informative narrower answer. Cochrane [chapter 10](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-10) supplies the quantitative best-known-line candidate; [chapter 12](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-12) supplies the competing non-meta-analysis route when its conditions fit. Their substantive question and interpretation rules justify the choice; intervention-review conventions do not govern every research family. The trade-off is model and grouping judgment in exchange for an interpretable answer. A changed target, dependence relation or defensible alternative model reopens that choice.

**How should missing contributions affect a finding?** The selected line locates what is missing and the particular inference it can change. Treating an available corpus as complete is cheaper but can hide selective results; rejecting every incomplete corpus would also erase bounded useful answers. **Adapt:** 4.1 and 4.3 retain question-relative coverage and distinguish unavailable, unreported, unsought and lost material. Cochrane [chapter 13](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-13) is a best-known-line candidate for these missing-evidence questions; its meta-analysis tools retain that scope. New eligible material, an identified selective omission or a stronger model of its effect reopens the affected finding.

**How can situated and mixed findings be related?** The selected line preserves context and finding-specific confidence, integrating transformed contributions only when they answer a shared question. The serious rival is separate synthesis of all quantitative and qualitative contributions; a different default would merge everything into one theme. Cochrane [chapter 21](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-21) supplies a best-known qualitative line and the separate-contribution choice; JBI [§8.3](https://jbi-global.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MANUAL/pages/355829259/8.3%2BThe%2BJBI%2Bapproach%2Bto%2Bmixed%2Bmethod%2Bsystematic%2Breviews) supplies the serious question-relative integration alternative. **Adapt:** 4.4 and 5.3 select between them by the question. This permits a useful shared answer while keeping different aspects separate and transformation losses recoverable. [GRADE-CERQual](https://www.cerqual.org/what-is-the-grade-cerqual-approach2/) supplies an applicable finding-level confidence candidate, not a numerical truth scale. The accepted cost is explicit interpretation and method choice. A changed tradition, question or stronger account of what transformation loses reopens the comparison.

**What can historical agreement establish?** The selected line compares source dependence, dating, purpose, contrary material and rival explanations. Narrative count is an attractive cheap default, but copied accounts cannot supply independent causal support. **Adapt:** 4.2–4.4 and 5.4 recover the shared memoir and the different contribution of the decision record. AHA [professional standards](https://www.historians.org/resource/statement-on-standards-of-professional-conduct/) supplies the best-known-line candidate for source integrity and evidence/interpretation discipline here; it supplies no verdict about the particular factory. The extra source criticism preserves the useful chronology while leaving the unsupported cause open. New provenance, dating or a substantive rival explanation reopens that inference.

These comparisons support different research traditions. Their combination here is question-relative guidance, not evidence that one synthesis procedure works universally.

### RMP.7:12 - Relations

RMP.10 can supply separately scoped candidate-practice accounts rather than an average of conflicting variants. RMP.11 develops diagnostic comparisons between specific historical accounts; this corpus synthesis supplies source contributions and dependence without claiming that a count of reports settles that comparison.

- **RMP.1–RMP.4** can supply the qualified question, design, operations and actual trace. Compatible direct inputs are equally usable; return only a missing or changed premise.
- **RMP.5** supplies examined source claims and receives a defeated individual inference. **RMP.6** supplies an actual credibility result when available or decides a useful further examination.
- **RMP.8** receives the synthesis when a wider claim or model must be revised or evidence returned to an actual receiving use. A sufficient bounded corpus answer can finish directly.
- **FPF F.1, F.0.1 and A.10**, with a qualified F.0.2 contribution when applicable, supply source selection, comparison and evidence-use relations. Their source work does not by itself establish this research synthesis.
- **Domain, access and receiving-practice Methods** supply their criteria, permissions and decisions. Research-Method improvement remains a distinct RMP.9/Core Method-development question.

### RMP.7:End


## RMP.8 - Use Research Results to Retain or Revise an Episteme's Claims and Return Bounded Evidence

> **Type:** Research Method Practice practitioner method pattern
> **Status:** Stable

### RMP.8:1 - Problem Frame

Use this pattern when research analysis, criticism, a credibility result or a synthesis changes what a knowledge account may assert, or when its recipient needs a bounded evidence return. Begin by locating **the exact claim, model assumption or explanatory relation that the supplied result can retain or change**.

A new laboratory synthesis can support a seal comparison while leaving its field-transfer premise unresolved. A dated archive record can defeat an attribution about a decision without explaining its cause or later implementation. A correction becomes useful when the earlier statement, new contribution and receiving use concern the same identified subject and conditions.

The result is an **EpistemeChangeAndEvidenceReturn**: the retained or changed knowledge contribution, its basis and limits, and the return needed by its actual use. A corrected sentence and short linked explanation can carry this result. A model with several dependent claims or a correction already relied on elsewhere may need a fuller account.

An episteme here is the identified knowledge account being revised: for example a claim, model, interpretation or pattern describing a Method and its use. RMP.8 concerns the asserted content of that account. A changed filename or publication label does not identify what its recipient should now believe or rely on.

Enter directly with a compatible supplied result from analysis, synthesis or criticism. An already sufficient RMP.5, RMP.6 or RMP.7 answer may finish at its own return. Use RMP.8 when a broader account or consequential receiving reliance needs reconciliation. The receiving practice supplies its decision criteria and authority; the same person can perform both contributions without merging them.

### RMP.8:2 - Problem

Research conclusions often change in transmission. A limited finding becomes a general recommendation; a criticism of one assumption is read as rejection of the whole model; a correction about one event silently replaces a claim about another. Conversely, an amended source can leave a known receiving use dependent on the earlier claim.

Another failure is to demand a new investigation whenever uncertainty remains. That postpones useful qualified answers and treats a proposed examination as evidence already obtained. A lack of feasible inquiry does not make the current account more credible.

The practitioner needs to identify the warranted change, carry it through the relevant account and return it with the limits that can change reliance.

### RMP.8:3 - Forces

| Force | Tension |
| --- | --- |
| Exact correction | A concise conclusion is useful, while a small change of subject, context or time can alter what was established. |
| Coherent models | A failed premise can affect several outputs, while unaffected claims should remain usable. |
| Receiving use | Evidence can change a practical choice, while the choice also depends on values, constraints and authority outside the research result. |
| Recoverability | Existing reliance may need the earlier statement and its correction, while every draft edit does not need a full change dossier. |
| Disclosure | A recipient needs enough basis to judge reliance, while source rights, confidentiality and community authority constrain access. |
| Presentation and content | Different publication forms can serve different readers, while a concise or familiar template can conceal a missing problem, rationale, operation or applicability condition. |
| Further inquiry | A valuable unanswered question may justify work, while useful completion and unobtainable acquisition remain possible. |

### RMP.8:4 - Solution

Match the supplied contribution to the earlier assertion, revise only what it warrants, reconcile the affected account and return the current answer to its actual use. Preserve the support, uncertainty and limits that matter to that return.

#### RMP.8:4.1 - Locate the assertion and its receiving question

Recover the earlier wording or model relation, its referents, comparison, context and time. State what result has arrived, what examination actually produced it, and which part of the account it bears on.

Ask whether the two sides concern the same claim. A factory's decision to close and its later closure are different events. A laboratory parameter and a field-use parameter can denote different conditions. A new finding about another population can be useful without contradicting the original bounded claim.

For an emerging account, identify the proposed contribution and what existing material it would add to or qualify. If there is no earlier claim to correct, state an addition rather than inventing a prior error.

Recover the receiving question when it changes how much explanation or assurance is needed. The question may be a scientific explanation, a reusable knowledge contribution or an engineering, public or personal use. Immediate operating benefit is not the only legitimate value of research.

If the source, subject correspondence or actual result is missing, return that specific gap. A selected credibility examination and a proposal for synthesis cannot serve as their performed results.

#### RMP.8:4.2 - State the warranted retention or change

Separate the contribution from a stronger claim the receiver might infer.

| Warranted disposition | What to state |
| --- | --- |
| Retain | The existing assertion still has its stated support under the examined conditions; identify the relevant new examination and its limits. |
| Narrow | Restrict the population, context, time, relation or transfer to what the result supports, preserving the supported part. |
| Qualify | Keep the identified assertion with the uncertainty, alternative explanation or reliance condition the result makes consequential. |
| Reject | Remove a defeated claim or inference and explain what defeats it. Rejection of one account does not establish a particular rival by default. |
| Add | State the new contribution and its relation to the existing account, including whether it is supported information, an interpretation or a hypothesis for further inquiry. |

Several dispositions may be needed for different claims in one model. Keep their distinct reasons. An increase in confidence needs an actual supporting contribution; repetition, a newer document date and unavailable criticism supply none by themselves.

Retain method-specific uncertainty. A numerical interval depends on its quantity and assumptions. A qualitative confidence judgment has its own grounds. “Uncertain” is too vague when the recipient needs to know that the unsupported step is causal attribution, extrapolation, prevalence or another particular inference.

An inconclusive result can leave the proposed effect unresolved. It does not automatically establish no effect or equivalence. Similarly, lack of access can limit what was examined without supplying evidence against the underlying claim.

#### RMP.8:4.3 - Reconcile the affected account

Follow the changed premise through the claims or outputs that actually rely on it. Identify which conclusions survive, which must change and which now need another supplied relation.

For a model, distinguish a represented target, structure, parameter, assumption, calculation and interpretation when the change bears on them differently. Correctly computed output can lose its warrant for a use when a transfer assumption fails. A locally supported parameter may remain useful within its calibration conditions.

Make consequential changes in the account itself, rather than leaving an unqualified conclusion beside a detached caveat. Preserve the earlier statement when an existing citation, correction or reliance requires recovery. For a draft that nobody has relied on, an ordinary edit with enough source connection can suffice.

A replacement explanation is a new assertion with its own support. If criticism only defeats the former explanation, retain the remaining alternatives without selecting one by elimination that the evidence does not warrant. Return a new research question or design choice through RMP.1 or RMP.2 as needed.

Use the existing records and source links that make this reasoning inspectable. RMP adds no compulsory change ledger for every account.

#### RMP.8:4.4 - Return evidence to the actual use

Lead with the current answer and what it changes for the named receiving question. Give the source or examination that supports it and the scope, uncertainty, dependence, transfer or access limit that can alter reliance.

When someone has already relied on the affected assertion, identify that actual use and provide the correction or limitation through its responsible owner and permitted route. FPF A.10.1 governs the general recovery and revalidation of affected uses; this Method supplies the research content to carry through that relation. A citation list may help locate reliance but does not prove that every citation used the changed claim.

The author of one account cannot silently replace another owner's record. A museum editor, model maintainer or receiving practitioner may need the corrected statement and its basis before changing their own account or decision. A known consequential return is not complete merely because the source text was edited. If required communication or access is unavailable, state the unfinished return and what would enable it while retaining the completed local correction.

Respect confidentiality, source rights, participant protection and applicable community authority. Use the least disclosure that supports the receiving question. A permitted redacted account may carry the conclusion; if it omits material necessary for a requested examination, state that examination limit. Do not imply that a public reader inspected protected originals.

The receiving practice then evaluates its available actions, values, constraints and authority. Research can narrow an action's evidential premise without selecting or authorizing that action.



##### RMP.8:4.4.1 - Make a research Method contribution recoverable across publication forms

Use this branch when the contribution includes a Method that another reader should understand, repeat, adapt or combine. First identify the knowledge contribution and the use to be supported; then choose how to present it.

A practitioner Method pattern is an episteme about a Method and its use. Its content includes the recurring difficulty, the situation in which that difficulty matters, competing forces, the solution and its grounds, worked applications, limits, consequences and relations. FPF's SoTA-Echoing adds the comparison with the current best-known line and serious alternatives that can change the Method. These are substantive claims and explanations, not decorations around an operation list. Apply A.3.2 when claiming that an episteme is a U.MethodDescription; filling a pattern template does not establish that membership.

Keep that content distinct from its publication form: the selected section template, natural language, notation, reading order, file arrangement, medium and place of publication. Translation or moving text between files may preserve the contribution; omitting a force that changes the choice of solution may not. A short entry can direct a reader to the developed account, but cannot supply an explanation that the account never contains.

An article can present several connected claims and Methods, their construction, evidence and limits. Its contributions may be developed into one pattern, several related patterns, an amendment of an existing language, or another suitable knowledge product. A pattern language organizes substantive problem-solution relations; a DPF has its own field of practice, promised coverage and maintenance boundary. Neither is merely an article layout or a collection of files. Do not infer one article–one pattern or one article–one DPF. E.4.DPF selects the framework contribution when that architectural choice matters.

For a pattern contribution, check the recurring problem–conditions–remedy relation as well as whether a suitably prepared recipient can reproduce its use. State what makes another situation an instance of that problem, which parts of the way of acting recur, which adaptations are permitted, what preparation and support are needed, and what result would count as successful use. Applying the Method again may produce a different artifact or numerical value while preserving its intended effect under the stated conditions. Recomputing one reported number alone does not establish this reusable reach. A correctly recognized limit is a useful boundary result; it is not a successful reproduction of the promised positive effect.

For a Method contribution, make the following connections usable:

1. **Recover the construction.** Explain the problem and frame, the objects and relations through which it is understood, the relevant forces and the resulting way of acting. Conceptual synthesis can combine, adapt or reinterpret already known Methods. Show both the horizontal organization—sequence, alternatives, feedback and returns—and the vertical relation between constituent actions and the larger Method where they change use. E.4.CM develops this composition; a bibliography of constituents does not establish their compatibility or supply missing joins.
2. **State what another reader is to repeat.** Reconstructing a derivation, rerunning a computation on the same inputs, obtaining new measurements and applying the Method under changed conditions test different claims. Say what is held comparable, what changes, the result to compare and what agreement means. Exact equality may be warranted for a derivation or deterministic calculation; new measurements usually require a justified uncertainty or agreement criterion. Use RMP.6 for the relevant credibility decision and for interpretation of an actual return. The word “reproduction” alone does not choose the examination.
3. **Provide the consequential means.** Supply or locate the definitions, assumptions, input preparation, reasoning, operations, data or material, comparison and interpretation needed for that examination. Specify versions, computational environment, randomization, calibration, timing or performer capability when a difference there can change the claim. For a reused Method, identify the usable source passage and the conditions supplied by it. A source title is insufficient when the reader still has to invent a missing operation. RMP.4 governs the actual trace; it cannot recover conduct for which no evidence survives.
4. **Choose and connect the presentations.** An empirical article may separate question, Methods, results and interpretation; a theoretical or Methods article may center a construction and its argument; a protocol or Stage 1 Registered Report describes proposed work, while a later results report states what was actually done and obtained. Use the applicable venue and study-type reporting requirements. A pattern presentation organizes the same supported contribution around recurring use, including problem frame, forces, solution, cases, boundaries and SoTA. Preserve the reasoning and evidence needed for that use even when section names and order change.
5. **Expose what is available and what remains untested.** Connect each presentation to the identifiable source contribution and the materials needed for its stated examination. State permitted access and consequential omissions. A protocol is not performed Work, an available artifact is not a successful rerun, and a repeatable calculation is not evidence for transfer of its model. Correct affected presentations and known receiving uses through 4.3–4.4 when their relied-on claims change.

Use the smallest explanation and access arrangement that supports the receiving use. A theoretical contribution need not invent an empirical dataset; protected participant material need not be made public contrary to its conditions of use. Conversely, a disclosure restriction can leave a particular public examination unavailable. State that limit rather than presenting the publication format as evidence of reproducibility.

#### RMP.8:4.5 - Finish the answer and select further inquiry only when warranted

Finish when the identified account has the warranted retention or change and the return required by its actual use is supplied, or when a precise input or delivery limit has been returned. A broader unresolved question does not automatically hold this bounded result open.

If further inquiry could materially improve an explanation, reusable finding or receiving decision, compare the attainable contribution with its whole burden. Include preparation, access, performance, interpretation, protection, shared resources and displaced work. An attractive experiment that cannot be obtained supplies no new evidence.

Use RMP.2 for a research-design choice and RMP.6 for a relevant credibility choice. A still-needed selection prevented by a missing input differs from a completed no-new-study allocation. Preserve that distinction and the current evidence limit. A worthwhile new possibility can later reopen the choice.

A recurring failure in how research Methods are selected or performed may identify an RMP.9 or Core Method-development question. State that need at its own available owner; it neither supplies a new Method-improvement result nor prevents the present knowledge contribution from being returned.

### RMP.8:5 - Archetypal Grounding

These constructed cases illustrate the Method rather than reporting actual research or completed communication.

#### RMP.8:5.1 - Keep the laboratory result, withdraw the unsupported field prediction

An engineer receives a synthesis supporting a positive mean difference in seal lifetime under specified accelerated laboratory conditions. The existing model account contains three contributions:

| Existing contribution | Supplied criticism and revision |
| --- | --- |
| The fitted wear relation describes the dry laboratory material over the tested range. | The supplied analysis still supports that bounded relation; retain its parameter, fit and uncertainty for that scope. |
| The same wear rate applies in the wet service environment. | The supplied synthesis concerns dry accelerated tests and does not establish this transfer; remove the account's claim that the research has demonstrated it. The transfer remains unresolved. |
| A service replacement time follows from the laboratory rate and the engineering wear limit. | The calculation may remain arithmetically correct, but its service interpretation relies on the unsupported transfer. Withdraw that field prediction as an established research conclusion. The supplied engineering limit remains the engineering owner's criterion. |

The return says: “The laboratory relation remains supported in its tested range. This research does not establish the wet-service wear rate or the replacement time derived from treating that rate as unchanged.” It includes the source result and the exact missing transfer premise.

A model with separate dry and wet rates is a possible next hypothesis, not a validated replacement supplied by this criticism. A useful and obtainable field comparison can be considered through RMP.2/RMP.6. The reliability owner receives the bounded evidence and retains the maintenance decision. A short correction to the model account can complete the research return even when the operational choice still needs more input.

#### RMP.8:5.2 - Correct the same historical event

Several later accounts claim that a public protest prompted the decision to close a factory. They share one retrospective memoir. An authenticated record dates that decision before the protest.

RMP.8 rejects the protest as the cause of that earlier decision, retains its supported timing and leaves the cause unresolved. Possible effects of the protest on later implementation remain a different question.

A museum description actually attributed the decision to the protest. Its responsible editor receives the corrected decision chronology, the source reference and the unresolved causal limit. The correction does not silently turn into a claim about why or when the physical closure occurred. Protected source detail stays within its access terms; if a public summary cannot support independent authentication, it says so.

If the same dated evidence were supplied against the broader claim “the protest affected the closure,” the return would instead distinguish the defeated decision-causation component from still-open implementation effects. Matching the event changes the warranted revision.

#### RMP.8:5.3 - Return a situated finding without inventing prevalence

A community synthesis links distrust in monitoring to withheld feedback in its examined settings. An earlier briefing says that this is the principal reason most local residents do not participate.

The supplied interpretive finding supports neither a population denominator nor the comparative frequency implied by “most” and “principal.” RMP.8 replaces the briefing's prevalence assertion with the situated contribution: withheld feedback contributed to distrust in the examined accounts, with the noted exceptions and contexts. The account distinguishes the source interpretations from the synthesist's broader explanation.

The community group can use that qualified insight when considering how to return monitoring information. The evidence does not establish how many residents would participate after a proposed change or authorize that change. A frequency survey is a separate research option if its attainable contribution warrants its burden.

#### RMP.8:5.4 - An adequate answer and a later correction

A requester receives an existing synthesis that already answers the specified comparison. A short linked answer with its applicability and uncertainty completes the return; there is no need to create a separate episteme-change form.

Later, an erratum reverses one result that materially supported the synthesis. Recover the affected finding and the known decision or account that relied on it. Recompute or reinterpret that finding through its supplying Method, revise its dependent claim and carry the correction to that actual use. Retain unaffected results. A newly observed date alone would not justify the same reopening.

#### RMP.8:5.5 - Valuable uncertainty without an obtainable study

A historical synthesis resolves a chronology but leaves a scientifically valuable mechanism unexplained. The only currently proposed inquiry requires records that cannot lawfully be accessed, and no worthwhile obtainable substitute is supplied.

The historian returns the supported chronology and unresolved mechanism and selects no further study for the current allocation. The explanation remains valuable and incomplete. If an accessible archive later supplies material capable of discriminating the live alternatives, its contribution and burden can justify a new research choice. Neither an immediate commercial payoff nor an unused continuation form is a prerequisite for the present answer.



#### RMP.8:5.6 - One calibration contribution, an article and a pattern

Consider a constructed contribution using the instrument relation y = a + bx, where x is the reference temperature and y the displayed temperature, both in degrees Celsius. Assume a separate instrument characterization supports an affine relation over 0–20 °C under the named operating conditions. The contribution does not establish that premise by fitting two points.

The reported reference pairs are (0, 2) and (20, 24). The reasoning gives b = (24 − 2)/(20 − 0) = 1.1 and a = 2; the correction is x = (y − 2)/1.1. A displayed 13 °C therefore gives 10 °C. A reader can reconstruct that derivation and recompute that result from the stated pairs. This repeats the calculation, not the original observations.

An article can present the instrument problem, the characterization it relies on, the derivation, actual observation procedure and data, and the scope of the conclusion. A pattern for correcting readings would explain when offset and scale errors defeat use, when the affine frame is justified, the tension between a simple correction and an unmodeled nonlinear response, how to obtain qualified references and apply the correction, and what to do when an independent comparison disagrees. Its cases, consequences, relations and SoTA comparison remain content. Retitling the equation “Solution” does not supply those missing explanations.

Now suppose the examination uses a newly obtained 10 °C reference and the instrument displays 13.2 °C. The corrected value is 10.1818… °C. Under a previously selected total agreement allowance of ±0.3 °C, with reference uncertainty included in that allowance, this observation agrees. That finding concerns this comparison; it does not establish every reading in the interval. RMP.6 retains the examination's actual scope.

This distinction also makes the pattern's repeatability testable. The same correction rule applies to another qualified reading; its output changes with that input. Recomputing 10 °C from the original display of 13 °C repeats the reported calculation. Applying the rule to the new display of 13.2 °C gives 10.1818… °C; copying the earlier answer would fail to repeat the Method. Recognition of the qualified affine frame and access to its calibration basis remain necessary on each use.

The pattern may be published in English and Russian, in separate files or in a single framework publication. Those choices need not change the calculation or its qualified frame. A shortened version that removes the 0–20 °C condition does change what a reader may infer. A proposed 40 °C application needs a new applicability basis; agreement at 10 °C cannot supply it. If a later investigation defeats the affine premise, RMP.8 preserves the arithmetic but revises the calibration claim in the article correction, affected pattern account and known receiving uses.

### RMP.8:6 - Bias-Annotation

A short correction is easiest to demonstrate in an account with one identifiable recipient. Distributed reliance, conflicting editions and protected sources can require more recovery and communication. Scale that work to the actual consequence instead of assuming that every research result needs a universal recipient register.

The engineering examples make decision support visible. Basic explanation, interpretation and reusable knowledge also have value. Preserve their legitimate questions when comparing future inquiry.

### RMP.8:7 - Conformance Checklist

Use these questions to examine the revised account and return:

- Do the earlier assertion, supplied contribution and claimed correction concern the same identified subject, context, comparison and time, or explicitly distinguished ones?
- Is each retained, narrowed, qualified, rejected or added contribution supported to the extent stated?
- Have affected model outputs or explanations been reconciled while unaffected contributions remain usable?
- Can the recipient recover the current answer, its basis, uncertainty and the limitation that changes reliance?
- Has a known consequential receiving use received the permitted correction, or is the exact unfinished return visible?
- Are obtained evidence, proposed inquiry and the receiver's decision authority distinct?
- When a Method contribution is returned for repetition or adaptation, can its recipient recover the substantive problem-solution account, the relevant examination and its means, independently of the chosen publication layout and language?

The working situation selects this Method. These questions examine the warranted content and actual return; recognizing a need for revision proves neither.

### RMP.8:8 - Common Anti-Patterns and How to Avoid Them

| Failure | What changes in practice |
| --- | --- |
| A new label substitutes for a changed assertion. | Locate and amend the actual claim, assumption or explanatory relation. |
| An article is converted into pattern headings and declared reproducible. | Preserve the substantive problem, frame, forces, construction, grounds and limits; provide the means for the named repetition and distinguish its actual result from mere availability. |
| A decision date is used as proof about physical closure. | Match the event or distinguish the decision from its later implementation before drawing the causal conclusion. |
| One failed premise erases the entire model. | Follow its actual dependencies, retaining supported parameters, observations and calculations within their remaining scope. |
| An unqualified conclusion survives beside a caveat. | Make the conclusion itself carry the warranted scope and reconcile the dependent outputs. |
| A local edit is assumed to correct known reliance. | Return the change through the actual receiver and authority, with an unresolved delivery limit when necessary. |
| Uncertainty automatically commissions research. | Compare the attainable contribution and whole burden; finish with the current limit when no further inquiry is selected. |

### RMP.8:9 - Consequences

The practitioner can preserve a useful research contribution while changing only what the evidence warrants. The recipient can distinguish a supported result from a stronger extrapolation, a defeated explanation and a future hypothesis.

The cost depends on the account's dependencies and actual reliance. A short current answer may suffice; an established model or consequential published correction can require recovery of prior meaning and a responsible return.

### RMP.8:10 - Rationale

A research result and its use are connected by particular assertions, assumptions and interpretations. Revising those connections prevents both overclaim and indiscriminate withdrawal.

Keeping the research contribution separate from receiving authority permits a useful answer even when the practical choice is unfinished. Keeping future inquiry separate from obtained evidence permits honest completion without denying the value of a longer research programme.

### RMP.8:11 - SoTA-Echoing

**What can this evidence change for its receiver?** The selected line returns a claim with the applicability and uncertainty that govern its use. The serious default is to turn a positive research result directly into a recommendation, or an inconclusive result into no effect. Cochrane [chapter 15](https://www.cochrane.org/authors/handbooks-and-manuals/handbook/current/chapter-15) supplies a best-known-line candidate because its interpretation distinctions expose both unsupported moves. **Adapt:** 4.2 and 4.4 carry the warranted assertion and its remaining inference limit while the receiving practice supplies further judgments. A short qualified answer retains the useful research result at lower burden than an unnecessary new study, but a consequential transfer limit requires explanation. A changed target, uncertainty, actual result or receiving use reopens that interpretation. Intervention-review guidance does not decide every domain's action.

**How should historical correction preserve its claim?** The selected line keeps evidence and interpretation connected to the same event and preserves contrary material and legitimate confidentiality. The attractive default is to update the broad narrative once a compelling dated source appears. That can substitute a decision for its implementation or treat a corrected date as a discovered cause. **Adapt:** 4.1–4.4 and 5.2 distinguish those events and return only the warranted correction. AHA [professional standards](https://www.historians.org/resource/statement-on-standards-of-professional-conduct/) supplies the best-known-line candidate for source integrity and evidence/interpretation discipline; the worked event comparison applies those principles rather than receiving a verdict from the standard. Recovering the event costs a small comparison and avoids a different unsupported historical claim. New dating, provenance or a changed asserted event reopens the inference.

**Which account and reliance should change?** The selected line identifies the affected claim or model relation, follows its actual dependencies and carries a consequential correction to the use that relied on it. Two plausible defaults are withdrawing the whole model after one failed premise or editing only the local source. They can respectively destroy supported knowledge or leave a receiving account dependent on the defeated claim. FPF C.2.1, A.10 and A.10.1 supply the governing episteme, evidence-use and affected-use distinctions and are the best-known-line candidates for this comparison. **Adapt:** 4.1, 4.3, 4.4 and 5.1 apply them to the research contribution, preserving the laboratory relation while correcting its unsupported field interpretation. The trade-off is dependency and receiving-use recovery proportional to actual reliance. This does not supply a universal registry or replace the generic Methods. Changed relied-on content or a newly identified consequential use reopens the relevant return.

**When is further inquiry worth obtaining?** The selected line compares attainable epistemic or practical contribution with whole burden and permits a bounded completed answer while uncertainty remains. The default of studying every open question can select unobtainable work; a rule requiring immediate operating payoff would discard valuable explanation. FPF C.11.DUA supplies the best-known-line candidate for this contribution/burden distinction, with RMP.2/RMP.6 supplying the actual research choice. **Adapt:** 4.5 and 5.5 preserve scientific value, shared resources, access and protection while keeping insufficient evidence distinct from no selected acquisition. This comparison costs judgment but avoids treating either resources or a proposal as evidence. Reopen when a worthwhile contribution becomes obtainable or an input changes a selection still needed.

**How can a reader repeat a published Method contribution?** The selected line couples a usable account of the Method to the particular examination and its obtainable materials. The tempting alternatives are to treat a paper's publication as sufficient for reproducibility, or to convert its steps into a pattern template while losing the problem, grounds and scope. Nature Portfolio's [reporting and availability policy](https://www.nature.com/ncomms/editorial-policies/reporting-standards) supplies a current publication-practice comparison: consequential design details and the access conditions for data, code, materials and protocols must be recoverable. The [Registered Reports description](https://www.cos.io/initiatives/registered-reports) supplies the specific distinction between assessment of proposed Methods and reporting obtained outcomes. **Adapt:** 4.4.1 and 5.6 connect those reporting concerns to RMP.4's actual trace, RMP.6's distinct credibility questions and FPF E.8's substantive pattern functions. The additional explanation serves the intended repetition or adaptation; it does not require every possible artifact for every inquiry. Neither reporting policy nor a complete template demonstrates a successful repetition. A missing consequential input, changed Method condition or failed actual comparison reopens the affected claim and presentation.

The external guidance contributes to bounded interpretation and research reporting; it does not empirically validate this cross-domain revision Method. A failed actual use or stronger methodological source can require a local repair.

### RMP.8:12 - Relations

- **RMP.5, RMP.6 and RMP.7** can supply compatible analysis, actual criticism or synthesis directly. Their sufficient short answers retain their own completion.
- **RMP.1 and RMP.2** receive a changed research question or design-selection need. **RMP.3 and RMP.4** retain the distinction between intended inquiry and actual material when it matters to the correction.
- **FPF C.2.1, A.10 and A.10.1** supply the underlying episteme, evidence-use and affected-use relations. **C.11.DUA** supplies the general useful-evidence and obtainable-inquiry comparison.
- **Receiving domain and practice Methods** supply action alternatives, values, safety, access, confidentiality and authority. A bounded research result informs those decisions.
- **RMP.9 and Core Method development** receive a distinct research-Method improvement difficulty through their actual available contributions.
- **FPF E.8** supplies the substantive functions of a pattern account and their publication conventions; **E.4.CM** supplies development of a composite Method contribution. **E.4.DPF** governs whether those contributions warrant a new or revised DPF; article layout alone cannot answer that question.

### RMP.8:End

# Part V - Improve and Refresh Research Methods and Practice


## RMP.9 — Decide Whether and How to Improve Research Methods and Practice

> **Status:** Stable

> **Type:** Research Method Practice practitioner method pattern

### RMP.9:0 - Use This When

Use this pattern when actual research work, criticism, a changed instrument or analytic tool, a new receiving situation, or learning within a field raises a concrete question about retaining or improving a research Method and its practice. Begin with the research use and what has become difficult or newly possible. Identify the object that needs attention and ask whether the available basis already supports retaining the Method or making a bounded correction.

The practical gain is an adequate Method kept in use, a justified change that reaches its actual users, or a clear limitation on an unsupported use. A known calculation error can be corrected without starting a Method-efficacy study. A materially changed research situation can justify a comparison when its possible results can change the decision and the whole effort is worthwhile.

Research-Method improvement is the branch of wider Method improvement governed here. Its particular concerns are the knowledge question, research validity and criticism, field-specific interpretation, actual research material and the claims that depend on the Method. Core supplies reusable Method identity, trial, fit, worth and variant contributions; A.3.1.MI supplies introduction when needed.

A disappointing finding, an unfamiliar technique, reviewer disagreement or a software release is a cue to inspect the question, not proof that the Method has failed. If only a particular analysis or knowledge claim needs correction, use RMP.5 or RMP.8. Return routine equipment recovery, institutional administration and permissions to their actual owners. Investigating a Method enters new research only when the RMP.1 research-membership conditions pass.

#### RMP.9:0.1 - Working Terms

| Term | Meaning for this use |
| --- | --- |
| research Method | The repeatable way of investigating, analysing, interpreting or criticizing a research question; its suitability depends on the question and conditions of use. |
| Method description | An account of how to use the Method. Correcting an ambiguous or erroneous account need not change the Method it describes. |
| implementation or support | The software, instrument, procedure support or other means used in applying the Method. A defect here may explain failed performance of an otherwise suitable Method. |
| semantic Method change | A change to what the Method requires or does that can alter its applicability or resulting claim. It raises a variant and qualification question. |
| supported retention | Keeping the Method or practice for the named conditions on an adequate existing basis. It establishes neither universal superiority nor adequacy for a new situation. |
| ResearchMethodPracticeRevision | The supported retention or change account returned by this pattern. It can report a retained Method, a bounded correction, a changed Method or a restricted/stopped use; its name does not assert that Method semantics changed. |

### RMP.9:1 - Problem Frame

A research team can encounter the same visible failure for different reasons. An uncertainty estimate can be wrong because a formula was implemented incorrectly, because observations violate its assumptions, or because the intended quantity changed. Correcting software addresses the first problem. New data do not automatically repair the second, and ranking estimators before settling the target can obscure the third.

Professional traditions also differ in what improvement means. A statistical comparison can examine coverage under relevant generating conditions. Reflexive qualitative analysis can need a more coherent interpretation, while a historical argument can need correction of a source transcription. A criterion useful for one purpose can distort another.

Improvement therefore starts with a situated question and a real alternative. Existing adequate practice, a limited correction, another Method, a situation-dependent variant and stopping an unsupported use can each be the strongest supported answer. Further inquiry is one possible contribution to that decision.

### RMP.9:2 - Problem

When every criticism is treated as a Method defect, teams replace useful practice and commission unnecessary trials. When every weakness is attributed to execution, an unsuitable Method survives. When improvement is judged by speed, agreement, novelty or a completed checklist alone, the research contribution can deteriorate while its chosen indicator improves.

There is a further trap in evidence acquisition. An unresolved comparison can generate a new protocol and reporting burden before anyone asks what its result could change or whether the comparison is attainable. Conversely, declining an expensive study can be mistaken for evidence that the present Method is adequate. The decision needs both a useful completion and an honest boundary on unsupported use.

### RMP.9:3 - Forces

| Force | Tension |
| --- | --- |
| Preserve useful practice | Familiarity is not evidence of adequacy, but a suitable Method should not be replaced merely because change is possible. |
| Locate the defect | Method, description, implementation, capability and receiving claim can fail differently; the visible symptom alone does not identify the correction. |
| Criticism within the research purpose | Shared demands for inspectability coexist with different statistical, interpretive and historical criteria. |
| Evidence and whole burden | A discriminating comparison can improve many later studies, while its design, conduct and uptake consume real research capacity. |
| Change and continuity | A useful revision must reach its users without transferring qualification evidence beyond its conditions or erasing consequential provenance. |

### RMP.9:4 - Solution

#### RMP.9:4.1 - Locate the question and try the supported present answer

Name the research use, the difficulty or opportunity, and what materially different answer would change in practice. Recover the relevant current Method, its description, actual application and receiving conditions far enough to distinguish the object at issue.

Check whether the observed failure comes from the reusable Method, its interpretation or implementation, a local deviation, unavailable capability or support, or an affected analysis or claim. Use the available evidence to make that distinction. A symptom that remains unexplained leaves the diagnosis open; it does not license a preferred replacement.

When an adequate present basis settles the question, use it. Retain the Method for its supported conditions, make the determinate correction, or return the bounded result to its owner. Verify the correction at the affected object and preserve the limits needed by whoever uses the result. Communicate this conclusion in the ordinary work result when that is sufficient.

**First useful example.** If a suitable Method calls for sample variance with denominator n−1 but its implementation uses n, fix and check that calculation. The Method can remain unchanged. Reanalyse the dependent results that used the wrong value; no new participants or efficacy trial are needed to determine the specified correction. The full case below shows the calculation and its reach.

#### RMP.9:4.2 - Compare alternatives for the same research use
